answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may transact, and let established peers attest to its work over time. A beacon registry publishes each bond and its history, so a newcomer must lock funds and earn endorsements before its trades carry weight. An attacker who spawns a lagoon of fake identities must fund every bond and wait out the probation for each one, while a single island of honest agents can flag and slash a misbehaving bond. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a thousand becomes a linear, auditable cost.
